description: A JavaScript engine: parser, bytecode interpreter, regexp engine, Unicode tables and standard library, de-identified so that no symbol, filename or banner ties it to an upstream release. Identifiers that take part in `##` token pasting (the atom, opcode and cfunc enumerations) keep their original spelling because the paste cannot be renamed consistently; everything else is renamed under one seeded mapping.
attacker_controls: the whole script text handed to JS_Eval and therefore every argument of every builtin it calls, every byte of the JSON text handed to JS_ParseJSON, the pattern and subject of every regular expression, and every byte of the buffer handed to JS_ReadObject

entry_points.why: the embedder hands it untrusted script source; every builtin the script can reach is downstream of it
parses attacker-supplied JSON text, byte for byte, before any application-level validation
compiles a regular expression pattern the script chooses, including its group names and quantifiers
runs compiled regexp bytecode against a subject string the script chooses
deserialises a byte buffer from outside the process into live objects, so every field is attacker-chosen

bugs.mechanism: The size handed to re_parse_group_name is sizeof(s->u.tmp_buf) plus UTF8_CHAR_LEN_MAX, four bytes more than the buffer really has. That callee treats buf_size as the hard end of the destination, so its own room check now permits an encode and a NUL that run off the end of tmp_buf and into the rest of the parser state, which lives on lre_compile's stack frame: an off-by-one stack buffer overflow.
bugs.attacker_control: the bytes of a named capture group in the regular expression source, whose last character can be a non-ASCII code point that encodes to four bytes

bugs.mechanism: The guard that the two hex digits after '%' are inside the string was relaxed from k + 2 >= p->len to k + 2 > p->len, so a percent escape truncated at the end of the input lets string_get_hex read index p->len: an out-of-bounds read one element past the JSString payload whose value decides the result.
bugs.attacker_control: the string passed to decodeURI/decodeURIComponent, in particular a trailing truncated %XX escape

bugs.mechanism: The backslash is no longer part of the escape set, so JS_ToQuotedString emits it raw into the quoted output. A value containing a backslash before a quote therefore serialises to text whose delimiters no longer match the input: the reader sees the quote as escaped and the string ends early, which is a delimiter injection into the serialised form.
bugs.attacker_control: the characters of any string reachable from the value being serialised, in particular backslash followed by a double quote

bugs.mechanism: The check that byte_length still fits in the remaining input was dropped, so the buffer constructor copies byte_length bytes from s->ptr with no upper bound at all: an unbounded copy that reads far past the end of the serialised input and hands the adjacent heap contents back as an ArrayBuffer.
bugs.attacker_control: the leb128 byte_length field of a serialised array buffer, up to 2^32-1, independently of how many bytes the input actually holds

bugs.mechanism: The error path frees the byte_code buffer but no longer frees group_names, which the success path does free, so every rejected pattern that got as far as recording a group name leaks that allocation: a resource leak an attacker grows without limit by compiling invalid patterns in a loop.
bugs.attacker_control: the regular expression source, including how many named groups appear before the syntax error that makes compilation fail

bugs.mechanism: The multi-byte branch now accepts j + utf8_encode_len(c) == dest_len instead of rejecting it, which fills the destination to its last byte and leaves j == dest_len, so the trailing 'if (j < dest_len) dest[j] = 0' never runs: the function returns a buffer with no NUL terminator, and its callers hand that buffer straight to %s.
bugs.attacker_control: the code points of the atom being formatted, so both its byte length and the encoded length of its last character

bugs.mechanism: The wide-string branch sizes the output at two bytes per UTF-16 code unit, but a code point in U+0800..U+FFFF encodes to three UTF-8 bytes, so a string of such characters writes one byte more per character than was allocated: a heap buffer overflow whose length and contents the string decides.
bugs.attacker_control: the contents of the string being converted, in particular how many of its code units are at or above U+0800

bugs.mechanism: The return value of expand_fast_array is ignored, but the next statement still sets p->u.array.count = len. When the allocation fails - which a length near 2^32 makes happen on demand - the object claims len elements over a values array that was never grown, and the copy loop then writes through p->u.array.u.values well past its end.
bugs.attacker_control: the length property of the receiver, which chooses the requested allocation size and so whether it fails

bugs.mechanism: The reference that keeps the pad string alive is dropped before the padding loop runs, so p1 - which points inside that JSString - is read after the string was freed. string_buffer_concat then copies from freed heap memory into the result, a use-after-free whose bytes end up in a string the caller can read back.
bugs.attacker_control: the pad argument, whose only reference is the one JS_ToString created when it is not already a string, and the target length that decides how many times the freed bytes are copied

bugs.mechanism: The array-buffer type check now leaves through the shared fail label after it has already released array_buffer, and that label releases it a second time. The extra JS_FreeValue drops a reference nobody holds, so the object is freed while it is still reachable from the reader's object table: a double free.
bugs.attacker_control: the tag of the value serialised in the array-buffer slot of a typed array, which decides whether the type check fails

bugs.mechanism: The bytecode permission check gained a second conjunct, s->error_state, which is zero on every path that reaches this tag, so the guard never fires and untrusted input reaches the function-bytecode reader even when the caller asked for bytecode to be refused.
bugs.attacker_control: the tag byte at the head of any serialised value, so the reader can be steered into the function-bytecode branch regardless of the caller's flags

bugs.mechanism: The decoder accepts a percent-encoded UTF-8 sequence in the surrogate range because the is_surrogate rejection was removed from the validity test. The invariant that a decoded string holds only scalar values is what lets the UTF-16 to UTF-8 conversion later assume every surrogate it sees is half of a pair, so a lone surrogate smuggled in this way re-encodes to a three-byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 at all, and the embedder receives it as if it were.
bugs.attacker_control: the percent escapes in the string handed to decodeURI/decodeURIComponent, including the ED A0..BF prefix that encodes a surrogate code point

bugs.mechanism: json_parse_value recurses once per nesting level and has no depth counter of its own; the only thing that stopped it was the stack-headroom test at the top of the tokeniser it calls on every step. With that test gone the recursion is unbounded and deeply nested input walks the C stack off its end instead of raising a stack overflow error.
bugs.attacker_control: the nesting depth of the JSON text, one recursion per '[' or '{', with no length limit other than the size of the input

bugs.mechanism: The re-clamp after the argument conversions now bounds final by len, the element count read before those conversions ran, instead of by the live p->u.array.count. Since final was already clamped to len the statement is a no-op, so a valueOf that shrinks a resizable buffer during conversion leaves final describing the old length while the memset writes into the new, smaller allocation: the value that was validated is not the one the write is bounded by.
bugs.attacker_control: a valueOf or toString callback on the fill arguments, which runs after len is captured and can resize the backing buffer before the write

bugs.mechanism: abuf->detached is tested before js_create_from_ctor, which reads new_target.prototype and therefore runs script that can detach the buffer, and the re-test afterwards was removed while the sibling re-test of offset against byte_length was kept. The view is then built over a data pointer that was freed between the check and the use, so every later access through it is a use-after-free.
bugs.attacker_control: a getter or Proxy trap on the prototype of the constructor passed as new.target, which executes inside js_create_from_ctor and can call transfer() on the buffer

decoys.safe_because: Bitwise OR is commutative and both operands are non-negative values of the same promoted type with no side effects, so the byte stored is bit-for-bit identical and nothing else observes the order of evaluation.
Every switch arm that reads v assigns it from get_u16 or get_u32 first, and the default arm aborts before any read, so on every path that reaches a use the initialiser has already been overwritten.
i is a size_t and therefore never negative, so the dominating i < dest_len already implies dest_len > 0; the added conjunct cannot be false when the first one is true.

allocated_size is the size of a live allocation, so it is far below SIZE_MAX/3 on any machine that could have returned it; size = allocated_size * 3 / 2 therefore always satisfies the added cap and the growth branch is taken exactly as before.
The two stores write different members of the same struct from constants, with no data or control dependence between them and no intervening read, so either order leaves identical state.

decoys.safe_because: The dominating test already returned for every len above JS_STRING_LEN_MAX, so a len above twice that value cannot reach the added branch; its guard is unsatisfiable at that point.

p is not reassigned in the loop and the string it points at is the read-only input, while the loop body only appends to a separate StringBuffer, so p->len is invariant and reading it once before the loop yields the same value on every iteration.

buf_start and buf_end are set once from the caller's buffer and its length and are never reassigned for the lifetime of the reader, so buf_start <= buf_end holds on every reachable path and the assertion can never fire.
v only ever holds the result of get_u16 or bswap16, both of which are at most 0xffff, so widening it to uint32_t cannot represent a value that the narrowing store into *pval would change.
chr is a fresh name with no other declaration in scope in this function or at file scope, and every occurrence of the old local is rewritten, so the same object is read and written in the same order.
